audit_findings.title: Forecast growth may belong partly to future shareholders
audit_findings.mechanism: Future equity issuance increases the share denominator and may finance part of the owner-earnings growth currently attributed entirely to 39.796132 million fully diluted shares.
audit_findings.evidence: Future long-term financing at GSWC and BVES will consist of both long-term debt and equity issuances in order to manage to the CPUC-authorized capital structure.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that equity is an intended component of long-term utility financing, and prior ATM issuance reduced first-half 2026 diluted EPS by $0.04. It does not establish the amount or timing of future AWR issuance; management presently reports no planned issuance through at least 2029. Nevertheless, the fixed-share base and bull cases capitalize 6%-8% growth, with 51.5%-52.6% of value in terminal value, so material post-2029 equity financing could make per-share growth substantially lower than modeled. This is a material unresolved model risk, not a demonstrated numerical error.
audit_findings.action: Build a financing schedule linking forecast capital expenditures, retained owner earnings, authorized debt/equity capital structures, and resulting AWR share issuance; rerun every scenario using annual diluted share counts.

audit_findings.title: Refundable developer advances may be an unbridged senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $80.926 million liability at 2026-06-30; a full deduction equals approximately $2.03 per share and 3.9% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Refund principal is a financing cash outflow that may escape an earnings-based OE numerator and is not separately deducted in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Advances for construction are generally refundable at a rate of 2.5% in equal annual installments over 40 years.
audit_findings.explanation: The repayment obligation is demonstrated, but an omission is not: developer-funded plant is excluded from rate base, and the related customer economics or recurring refunds may already be reflected in normalized OE. Even treating the entire latest liability as an additional equity claim would reduce base value from $52.54 to about $50.51 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $88.53 market price. That gross treatment is also more severe than the scheduled 40-year refunds.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile advance receipts and refunds for every OE year, determine whether normalized OE already bears the refunds, and either forecast the annual net cash flows or deduct only the present value not otherwise captured.

audit_findings.title: Historical stability predates a material regulatory regime change
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the affected water segment supplied $100.946 million, or 77.4%, of 2025 consolidated net income
audit_findings.mechanism: The loss of full revenue and supply-cost decoupling can change normalized OE variability and the sustainable growth assumptions used in the forecast and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: However, without the continuation of a full revenue decoupling mechanism such as the WRAM and a full supply cost decoupling balancing account such as the MCBA, Registrant may be subject to future volatility in revenues and earnings as a result of fluctuations in water consumption by our customers and changes in water supply cost mix.
audit_findings.explanation: The regulatory change is demonstrated and affects the company's dominant earnings segment. The filing also states that the combined 2025 consumption and supply-mix effect was not material, while 2026 results show both favorable and unfavorable movements under the new regime. The available record therefore demonstrates greater exposure but does not quantify a sustainable downside or show that the 6%-8% growth cases are wrong. Materiality remains unresolved rather than demonstrated.
audit_findings.action: Separate the 2025 and 2026 earnings effects of consumption variance and source-mix variance, normalize OE under M-WRAM and ICBA economics, and rerun explicit adverse-consumption and purchased-water-mix scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Retirement-trust investment gains may contaminate operating OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.511 million in 2025, $5.293 million in 2024, and $5.008 million in 2023; the 2025 amount is 4.4% of the $124.8 million anchor, but the valuation effect is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If trust investment gains remain in OE, market returns are capitalized as operating earnings even though the related trust assets and matched retirement obligation are outside the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, other income (net of other expense) increased due primarily to gains of $5.5 million generated on investments held to fund one of the Company’s retirement plans as compared to gains of $5.3 million recorded in 2024, due to financial market conditions.
audit_findings.explanation: The gains and their inclusion in reported net income are demonstrated, but the record does not show whether the OE construction removed them. Cash-flow statements reverse these gains when reconciling net income to operating cash flow, so contamination depends on the undisclosed OE calculation path. Earlier trend years and the appropriate tax effect are also unavailable, preventing a reliable materiality calculation.
audit_findings.action: Produce the year-by-year OE reconciliation and verify removal of all realized and unrealized retirement-trust returns; if they remain, remove them, refit the trend anchor, and rerun all scenarios or add the trust assets net of the matched obligation to the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Customer-dedicated PFAS proceeds may be counted as shareholder cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $16.851 million regulatory liability at 2026-06-30; a full deduction equals approximately $0.42 per share and 0.8% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Customer-dedicated settlement proceeds may be included in the $21.657 million cash bridge even though the corresponding regulatory liability requires future customer-benefiting expenditures or offsets.
audit_findings.evidence: The amounts in the memorandum account have been recorded as a regulatory liability that is being used to offset the incremental investments in replacement and treatment of property, as well as operations and maintenance expenses and other direct expenses related to PFAS contamination.
audit_findings.explanation: The customer obligation is demonstrated, but the amount of dedicated proceeds still present in cash is not. Using the entire $16.851 million regulatory liability as a conservative bridge deduction would reduce base value from $52.54 to about $52.12 per share, which is too small to change the valuation conclusion relative to the $88.53 market price. Some proceeds may already have been spent or remain receivable, making the actual overlap smaller.
audit_findings.action: Trace each PFAS receipt, receivable, expenditure, and memorandum-account offset through 2026-06-30; remove from bridge cash the remaining dedicated cash unless its future use is already deducted in OE.

audit_findings.title: The trend anchor may retain a one-time 2024 tax benefit
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.0 million filed benefit; even a conservative one-for-one $5.0 million anchor reduction would lower base value by approximately $82.9 million, $2.08 per share, or 4.0%
audit_findings.mechanism: A nonrecurring tax benefit retained in 2024 OE raises the fitted log trend and therefore the anchor applied to every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Included in the consolidated results for 2024 was a tax benefit of $5.0 million, or $0.13 per share, resulting from the final decision issued by the CPUC on January 30, 2025 in connection with GSWC’s latest general rate case proceeding.
audit_findings.explanation: The benefit is demonstrated, but its retention in the OE series is not. As a conservative scale test, reducing the $124.8 million anchor directly by the entire $5.0 million—more severe than the effect expected from correcting one observation in a ten-year trend—would lower base value from $52.54 to about $50.46 per share. It would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $88.53 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the 2024 OE reconciliation; if the benefit remains, reduce 2024 OE by $5.0 million, refit the ten-year log trend, reapply the MIN(trend, latest) rule, and rerun all scenarios.
